title: Domestic airline duopoly
summary: Two airline groups, Qantas (with Jetstar) and Virgin Australia, carry about 98% of domestic passengers after Bonza collapsed and Rex left capital-city routes in 2024. The ACCC has linked reduced domestic competition to the groups' significant earnings.
direction_rationale: With two groups left, there is little pressure on fares, and slots at congested airports, aircraft and scale make entry hard.

industries.name: Airport Operations and Other Air Transport Support Services

verified.notes: A market structure, not a law: no dates. ACCC pages refuse automated requests; the findings are from search excerpts of the ACCC's report and press coverage, not read in full. The 98% share is from the ACCC's 2025 domestic airline competition reporting.

assessment.summary: Two airline groups carry almost all domestic passengers, after two challengers failed in 2024. Fares face little competitive pressure, and new entrants struggle to get slots and scale.

marks.reason: Two groups carry about 98% of domestic passengers.
